category: Scripting: oEditor Geometry, Properties, Coordinate Systems, Import/Export & Definition Manager
description: The native 3D Modeler editor object (oEditor = oDesign.SetActiveEditor("3D Modeler")) commands beyond the box/cylinder/polyline/unite/subtract calls already catalogued: remaining primitives and the equation curve, every boolean and transform, sweeps and sheet/solid conversions, attribute and command-history edits through ChangeProperty, geometry queries by ID, selections and named lists, coordinate systems, CAD import/export, model units and history control, plus the oDefinitionManager material commands. Every call takes the nested name/value arrays that Tools > Record Script To File writes; the IronPython/CPython list form is shown.

tools.name: oEditor.CreateSphere / oEditor.CreateCone / oEditor.CreateCircle
tools.description: Remaining primitive commands of the 3D Modeler: a sphere from centre and radius, a cone (or frustum) from base centre, axis, height and two radii, and a circle sheet or line from centre, radius, axis and optional segment count. Each takes a parameters array and the common Attributes array (name, colour, transparency, coordinate system, material, solve-inside, shell element), and returns the created object's name.
tools.usage:
name = oEditor.CreateSphere(["NAME:SphereParameters", "XCenter:=", "0mm", "YCenter:=", "0mm", "ZCenter:=", "0mm", "Radius:=", "10mm"], <Attributes>)
name = oEditor.CreateCone(["NAME:ConeParameters", "XCenter:=", "0mm", "YCenter:=", "0mm", "ZCenter:=", "0mm", "WhichAxis:=", "Z", "Height:=", "20mm", "BottomRadius:=", "5mm", "TopRadius:=", "0mm"], <Attributes>)
name = oEditor.CreateCircle(["NAME:CircleParameters", "IsCovered:=", True, "XCenter:=", "0mm", "YCenter:=", "0mm", "ZCenter:=", "0mm", "Radius:=", "2mm", "WhichAxis:=", "Z", "NumSegments:=", "0"], <Attributes>)

parameters.name: Attributes array
parameters.description: ["NAME:Attributes", "Name:=", "Sphere1", "Flags:=", "", "Color:=", "(143 175 143)", "Transparency:=", 0, "PartCoordinateSystem:=", "Global", "UDMId:=", "", "MaterialValue:=", "\"vacuum\"", "SurfaceMaterialValue:=", "\"\"", "SolveInside:=", True, "ShellElement:=", False, "ShellElementThickness:=", "0mm", "IsMaterialEditable:=", True, "UseMaterialAppearance:=", False, "IsLightweight:=", False]

parameters.name: MaterialValue
parameters.description: Material name wrapped in escaped double quotes inside the string, e.g. "\"copper\"".

parameters.name: WhichAxis
parameters.description: "X", "Y" or "Z" in the working coordinate system.

parameters.name: NumSegments
parameters.description: "0" for a true circle, otherwise the polygon side count (string).

tools.example:
import ScriptEnv
ScriptEnv.Initialize("Ansoft.ElectronicsDesktop")
oProject = oDesktop.GetActiveProject(); oDesign = oProject.GetActiveDesign()
oEditor = oDesign.SetActiveEditor("3D Modeler")
attrs = ["NAME:Attributes", "Name:=", "Lens", "Flags:=", "", "Color:=", "(143 175 143)", "Transparency:=", 0.5,
         "PartCoordinateSystem:=", "Global", "UDMId:=", "", "MaterialValue:=", "\"Rexolite\"", "SurfaceMaterialValue:=", "\"\"",
         "SolveInside:=", True, "ShellElement:=", False, "ShellElementThickness:=", "0mm", "IsMaterialEditable:=", True,
         "UseMaterialAppearance:=", False, "IsLightweight:=", False]
oEditor.CreateSphere(["NAME:SphereParameters", "XCenter:=", "0mm", "YCenter:=", "0mm", "ZCenter:=", "0mm", "Radius:=", "R_lens"], attrs)
oEditor.CreateCircle(["NAME:CircleParameters", "IsCovered:=", True, "XCenter:=", "-L", "YCenter:=", "0mm", "ZCenter:=", "0mm",
                      "Radius:=", "r_out", "WhichAxis:=", "X", "NumSegments:=", "0"],
                     ["NAME:Attributes", "Name:=", "PortSheet", "Flags:=", "", "Color:=", "(143 175 143)", "Transparency:=", 0,
                      "PartCoordinateSystem:=", "Global", "UDMId:=", "", "MaterialValue:=", "\"vacuum\"", "SurfaceMaterialValue:=", "\"\"",
                      "SolveInside:=", True, "ShellElement:=", False, "ShellElementThickness:=", "0mm", "IsMaterialEditable:=", True,
                      "UseMaterialAppearance:=", False, "IsLightweight:=", False])
tools.notes: Attribute keys grow with releases (UDMId, IsLightweight arrived later); AEDT tolerates missing keys and uses defaults. PyAEDT equivalents: hfss.modeler.create_sphere / create_cone / create_circle. Also available: CreateEllipse, CreateRegularPolygon, CreateRegularPolyhedron, CreateTorus, CreateHelix, CreateSpiral, CreateBondwire.

tools.name: oEditor.CreateRegion
tools.description: Create the auto-sizing air Region around the model with per-direction padding types and values (Percentage Offset, Absolute Offset, Absolute Position, Transverse Percentage Offset). The Region is the object radiation, PML and FE-BI boundaries are assigned to; its attributes set the material (vacuum) and solve-inside flag.
tools.usage:
oEditor.CreateRegion(["NAME:RegionParameters",
    "+XPaddingType:=", "Percentage Offset", "+XPadding:=", "300", "-XPaddingType:=", "Percentage Offset", "-XPadding:=", "300",
    "+YPaddingType:=", "Percentage Offset", "+YPadding:=", "300", "-YPaddingType:=", "Percentage Offset", "-YPadding:=", "300",
    "+ZPaddingType:=", "Absolute Offset", "+ZPadding:=", "30mm", "-ZPaddingType:=", "Absolute Offset", "-ZPadding:=", "0mm"],
    ["NAME:Attributes", "Name:=", "Region", "Flags:=", "Wireframe#", "Color:=", "(143 175 143)", "Transparency:=", 0, "PartCoordinateSystem:=", "Global", "UDMId:=", "", "MaterialValue:=", "\"vacuum\"", "SurfaceMaterialValue:=", "\"\"", "SolveInside:=", True, "ShellElement:=", False, "ShellElementThickness:=", "0mm", "IsMaterialEditable:=", True, "UseMaterialAppearance:=", False, "IsLightweight:=", False])

parameters.name: <dir>PaddingType
parameters.description: "Percentage Offset" (of the model size), "Absolute Offset", "Absolute Position" or "Transverse Percentage Offset" for each of the six directions.

parameters.name: <dir>Padding
parameters.description: Numeric string (percent) or length with units, expressions allowed.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.description: "Wireframe#" displays the region as wireframe.

tools.example:
oEditor.CreateRegion(["NAME:RegionParameters", "+XPaddingType:=", "Absolute Offset", "+XPadding:=", "lambda0/4",
    "-XPaddingType:=", "Absolute Offset", "-XPadding:=", "lambda0/4", "+YPaddingType:=", "Absolute Offset", "+YPadding:=", "lambda0/4",
    "-YPaddingType:=", "Absolute Offset", "-YPadding:=", "lambda0/4", "+ZPaddingType:=", "Absolute Offset", "+ZPadding:=", "lambda0/4",
    "-ZPaddingType:=", "Absolute Offset", "-ZPadding:=", "0mm"],
    ["NAME:Attributes", "Name:=", "Region", "Flags:=", "Wireframe#", "Color:=", "(143 175 143)", "Transparency:=", 0,
     "PartCoordinateSystem:=", "Global", "UDMId:=", "", "MaterialValue:=", "\"vacuum\"", "SurfaceMaterialValue:=", "\"\"",
     "SolveInside:=", True, "ShellElement:=", False, "ShellElementThickness:=", "0mm", "IsMaterialEditable:=", True,
     "UseMaterialAppearance:=", False, "IsLightweight:=", False])
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignRadiation(["NAME:Rad1", "Objects:=", ["Region"]])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.modeler.create_region(pad_value, pad_type). Region padding is edited later with ChangeProperty on the Geometry3DCmdTab of "Region:CreateRegion:1". Only one Region object per design; use a box for additional air volumes.

tools.name: oEditor.CreateEquationCurve
tools.description: Draw a parametric curve from X(t), Y(t), Z(t) expressions in the parameter _t over [tStart, tEnd], optionally discretised into a number of points and given a polyline cross-section. The native form of Draw > Equation Based Curve used for log-spirals, tapers and sinuous shapes.
tools.usage:
oEditor.CreateEquationCurve(["NAME:EquationBasedCurveParameters", "XtFunction:=", "<expr>", "YtFunction:=", "<expr>", "ZtFunction:=", "<expr>",
    "tStart:=", "0", "tEnd:=", "1", "NumOfPointsOnCurve:=", "0", "Version:=", 1,
    ["NAME:PolylineXSection", "XSectionType:=", "None", "XSectionOrient:=", "Auto", "XSectionWidth:=", "0", "XSectionTopWidth:=", "0", "XSectionHeight:=", "0", "XSectionNumSegments:=", "0", "XSectionBendType:=", "Corner"]],
    ["NAME:Attributes", "Name:=", "EquationCurve1", "Flags:=", "", "Color:=", "(143 175 143)", "Transparency:=", 0, ...])

parameters.name: XtFunction / YtFunction / ZtFunction
parameters.description: Expressions in _t, e.g. "r0*exp(a*_t)*cos(_t)"; angles in radians unless units are written.

parameters.name: tStart / tEnd
parameters.description: Parameter limits as strings.

parameters.name: NumOfPointsOnCurve
parameters.description: "0" keeps an analytic curve; N gives a polyline with N vertices.

parameters.name: PolylineXSection
parameters.description: "None", "Line", "Circle", "Rectangle", "Isosceles Trapezoid" with width/height/segment/bend settings.

tools.example:
oEditor.CreateEquationCurve(["NAME:EquationBasedCurveParameters",
    "XtFunction:=", "r0*exp(0.2*_t)*cos(_t)", "YtFunction:=", "r0*exp(0.2*_t)*sin(_t)", "ZtFunction:=", "0",
    "tStart:=", "0", "tEnd:=", "4*pi", "NumOfPointsOnCurve:=", "400", "Version:=", 1,
    ["NAME:PolylineXSection", "XSectionType:=", "Rectangle", "XSectionOrient:=", "Z", "XSectionWidth:=", "0.5mm",
     "XSectionTopWidth:=", "0mm", "XSectionHeight:=", "0.035mm", "XSectionNumSegments:=", "0", "XSectionBendType:=", "Corner"]],
    ["NAME:Attributes", "Name:=", "SpiralArm", "Flags:=", "", "Color:=", "(143 175 143)", "Transparency:=", 0,
     "PartCoordinateSystem:=", "Global", "UDMId:=", "", "MaterialValue:=", "\"copper\"", "SurfaceMaterialValue:=", "\"\"",
     "SolveInside:=", True, "ShellElement:=", False, "ShellElementThickness:=", "0mm", "IsMaterialEditable:=", True,
     "UseMaterialAppearance:=", False, "IsLightweight:=", False])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.modeler.create_equationbased_curve(...). CreateEquationSurface exists for parametric surfaces (u, v). The curve stays editable in the history tree (Properties window shows the functions).

tools.name: oEditor.Intersect / oEditor.Split
tools.description: Boolean intersection of the selected objects (first object keeps its name and material) and splitting of objects by a coordinate plane of the working CS or by a tool face/edge, keeping both sides or one. The Split parameter array chooses the plane, the side to keep, the tool type and whether to split only crossing objects and delete invalid results.
tools.usage:
oEditor.Intersect(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Sphere1,Cylinder1"], ["NAME:IntersectParameters", "KeepOriginals:=", False])
oEditor.Split(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Box1", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"],
              ["NAME:SplitToParameters", "SplitPlane:=", "XY", "WhichSide:=", "PositiveOnly", "ToolType:=", "PlaneTool",
               "ToolEntityID:=", -1, "SplitCrossingObjectsOnly:=", False, "DeleteInvalidObjects:=", True])

parameters.name: Selections
parameters.description: Comma-separated object names (no spaces).

parameters.name: KeepOriginals
parameters.description: True clones the inputs before intersecting.

parameters.name: SplitPlane / WhichSide
parameters.description: "XY", "YZ", "ZX" (or "Dummy" with a tool) and "Both", "PositiveOnly", "NegativeOnly".

parameters.name: ToolType / ToolEntityID
parameters.description: "PlaneTool" with -1, or "FaceTool"/"EdgeTool" with the entity ID.

tools.example:
oEditor.Intersect(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Lens,Cyl"], ["NAME:IntersectParameters", "KeepOriginals:=", False])
# keep the x>0 half of horn and region for a symmetry model
oEditor.Split(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Horn,Region", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"],
              ["NAME:SplitToParameters", "SplitPlane:=", "YZ", "WhichSide:=", "PositiveOnly", "ToolType:=", "PlaneTool",
               "ToolEntityID:=", -1, "SplitCrossingObjectsOnly:=", False, "DeleteInvalidObjects:=", True])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.modeler.intersect / split. The split plane passes through the working CS origin - call SetWCS or CreateRelativeCS first to cut elsewhere. Objects with "Both" get a _Split suffix for the second half.

tools.name: oEditor.Move / oEditor.Rotate / oEditor.Scale / oEditor.Mirror
tools.description: Rigid transforms added to the history of the selected objects: translate by a vector, rotate about a working-CS axis, scale about the working-CS origin, and mirror about a plane defined by a base point and a normal. Values may be expressions so the placement stays parametric; the transforms are recorded as Move/Rotate/Scale/Mirror history items editable in the Properties window.
tools.usage:
oEditor.Move(sel, ["NAME:TranslateParameters", "TranslateVectorX:=", "10mm", "TranslateVectorY:=", "0mm", "TranslateVectorZ:=", "0mm"])
oEditor.Rotate(sel, ["NAME:RotateParameters", "RotateAxis:=", "Z", "RotateAngle:=", "30deg"])
oEditor.Scale(sel, ["NAME:ScaleParameters", "ScaleX:=", "2", "ScaleY:=", "2", "ScaleZ:=", "1"])
oEditor.Mirror(sel, ["NAME:MirrorParameters", "MirrorBaseX:=", "0mm", "MirrorBaseY:=", "0mm", "MirrorBaseZ:=", "0mm", "MirrorNormalX:=", "1mm", "MirrorNormalY:=", "0mm", "MirrorNormalZ:=", "0mm"])
# sel = ["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Box1,Box2", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"]

parameters.name: TranslateVectorX/Y/Z
parameters.description: Translation components with units or expressions.

parameters.name: RotateAxis / RotateAngle
parameters.description: "X", "Y", "Z" of the working CS and the angle with units.

parameters.name: ScaleX/Y/Z
parameters.description: Scale factors as strings.

parameters.name: MirrorBase* / MirrorNormal*
parameters.description: Point on the mirror plane and its normal vector (components carry length units in recorded scripts).

tools.example:
sel = ["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Connector", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"]
oEditor.Move(sel, ["NAME:TranslateParameters", "TranslateVectorX:=", "x_conn", "TranslateVectorY:=", "0mm", "TranslateVectorZ:=", "h_pcb"])
oEditor.Rotate(sel, ["NAME:RotateParameters", "RotateAxis:=", "Z", "RotateAngle:=", "rot_conn"])
oEditor.Mirror(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "DipoleArm", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"],
               ["NAME:MirrorParameters", "MirrorBaseX:=", "0mm", "MirrorBaseY:=", "0mm", "MirrorBaseZ:=", "0mm",
                "MirrorNormalX:=", "1mm", "MirrorNormalY:=", "0mm", "MirrorNormalZ:=", "0mm"])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.modeler.move / rotate / scale / mirror. Scale is about the working coordinate system origin, not the object centre. DuplicateMirror creates a mirrored copy instead of moving the original.

tools.name: oEditor.DuplicateAroundAxis / oEditor.DuplicateMirror
tools.description: Create linked copies of objects: DuplicateAroundAxis produces NumClones rotational copies at AngleStr increments about a working-CS axis, DuplicateMirror creates one mirrored copy about a plane. Both accept the Options array that duplicates boundary/excitation assignments to the copies and an optional flag to group the new objects, and return the new object names.
tools.usage:
names = oEditor.DuplicateAroundAxis(sel, ["NAME:DuplicateAroundAxisParameters", "CreateNewObjects:=", True, "WhichAxis:=", "Z", "AngleStr:=", "45deg", "NumClones:=", "8"],
                                    ["NAME:Options", "DuplicateAssignments:=", True], ["CreateGroupsForNewObjects:=", False])
names = oEditor.DuplicateMirror(sel, ["NAME:DuplicateToMirrorParameters", "DuplicateMirrorBaseX:=", "0mm", "DuplicateMirrorBaseY:=", "0mm", "DuplicateMirrorBaseZ:=", "0mm",
                                      "DuplicateMirrorNormalX:=", "1mm", "DuplicateMirrorNormalY:=", "0mm", "DuplicateMirrorNormalZ:=", "0mm"],
                                ["NAME:Options", "DuplicateAssignments:=", False], ["CreateGroupsForNewObjects:=", False])

parameters.name: CreateNewObjects
parameters.description: True makes independent objects; False keeps the clones as one multi-body object.

parameters.name: WhichAxis / AngleStr / NumClones
parameters.description: Axis, angular step and total count including the original (strings; expressions allowed).

parameters.name: DuplicateAssignments
parameters.description: Copy boundaries and excitations to the clones (ports get new names).

parameters.name: CreateGroupsForNewObjects
parameters.description: Put the new objects in a group.

tools.example:
sel = ["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Element", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"]
new = oEditor.DuplicateAroundAxis(sel, ["NAME:DuplicateAroundAxisParameters", "CreateNewObjects:=", True, "WhichAxis:=", "Z",
                                        "AngleStr:=", "360deg/n_elem", "NumClones:=", "n_elem"],
                                  ["NAME:Options", "DuplicateAssignments:=", True], ["CreateGroupsForNewObjects:=", False])
oDesktop.AddMessage(oProject.GetName(), oDesign.GetName(), 0, "created: " + ",".join(new))
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.modeler.duplicate_around_axis / duplicate_and_mirror; DuplicateAlongLine is catalogued with Unite/Subtract. The return value is the list of new names (empty when CreateNewObjects is False).

tools.name: oEditor.SweepAlongVector / oEditor.SweepAroundAxis / oEditor.SweepAlongPath
tools.description: Sweep 1D/2D objects into sheets/solids: along a vector with draft angle and draft type, around a working-CS axis by an angle with optional faceting, or along a path polyline (selected together with the profile) with draft and twist. These are the native Draw > Sweep operations used for extrusions with draft, revolved bodies and routed cables/waveguides.
tools.usage:
oEditor.SweepAlongVector(sel, ["NAME:VectorSweepParameters", "DraftAngle:=", "0deg", "DraftType:=", "Round", "CheckFaceFaceIntersection:=", False, "SweepVectorX:=", "0mm", "SweepVectorY:=", "0mm", "SweepVectorZ:=", "12mm"])
oEditor.SweepAroundAxis(sel, ["NAME:AxisSweepParameters", "DraftAngle:=", "0deg", "DraftType:=", "Round", "CheckFaceFaceIntersection:=", False, "SweepAxis:=", "Z", "SweepAngle:=", "360deg", "NumOfSegments:=", "0"])
oEditor.SweepAlongPath(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Profile,Path", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"],
                       ["NAME:PathSweepParameters", "DraftAngle:=", "0deg", "DraftType:=", "Round", "CheckFaceFaceIntersection:=", False, "TwistAngle:=", "0deg"])

parameters.name: DraftAngle / DraftType
parameters.description: Draft in degrees and "Round", "Natural" or "Extended" corner handling.

parameters.name: SweepVectorX/Y/Z
parameters.description: Extrusion vector components.

parameters.name: SweepAxis / SweepAngle / NumOfSegments
parameters.description: Revolution axis, angle and number of facets ("0" = smooth).

parameters.name: Selections for path sweep
parameters.description: Profile and path object names together; the path must be a polyline.

parameters.name: TwistAngle
parameters.description: Total twist along the path.

tools.example:
oEditor.SweepAlongVector(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "PatchOutline", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"],
    ["NAME:VectorSweepParameters", "DraftAngle:=", "0deg", "DraftType:=", "Round", "CheckFaceFaceIntersection:=", False,
     "SweepVectorX:=", "0mm", "SweepVectorY:=", "0mm", "SweepVectorZ:=", "t_cu"])
oEditor.SweepAroundAxis(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "HornHalf", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"],
    ["NAME:AxisSweepParameters", "DraftAngle:=", "0deg", "DraftType:=", "Round", "CheckFaceFaceIntersection:=", False,
     "SweepAxis:=", "Z", "SweepAngle:=", "360deg", "NumOfSegments:=", "0"])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.modeler.sweep_along_vector / sweep_around_axis / sweep_along_path. A profile that crosses the revolution axis produces an invalid body; keep it on one side.

tools.name: oEditor.ThickenSheet / oEditor.CoverLines / oEditor.CoverSurfaces / oEditor.DetachFaces / oEditor.SectionAlongPlane
tools.description: Sheet and face utilities: thicken a sheet into a solid (one or both sides), cover closed polylines into sheets and cover open shells into solids, detach chosen faces from an object into new sheet objects, and section an object with a plane producing intersection sheets. These commands generate port sheets, integration surfaces and field-plot planes that remain linked to the parent geometry.
tools.usage:
oEditor.ThickenSheet(sel, ["NAME:SheetThickenParameters", "Thickness:=", "0.035mm", "BothSides:=", False])
oEditor.CoverLines(sel)
oEditor.CoverSurfaces(sel)
oEditor.DetachFaces(sel, ["NAME:Parameters", ["NAME:DetachFacesToParameters", "FacesToDetach:=", [68, 67]]])
oEditor.Section(sel, ["NAME:SectionToParameters", "CreateNewObjects:=", True, "SectionPlane:=", "YZ", "SectionCrossObject:=", False])

parameters.name: Thickness / BothSides
parameters.description: Extrusion distance (negative reverses) and symmetric thickening.

parameters.name: FacesToDetach
parameters.description: List of face IDs (from GetFaceIDs or a recorded selection).

parameters.name: SectionPlane / SectionCrossObject
parameters.description: "XY", "YZ", "ZX" of the working CS; True sections all objects crossing the plane.

tools.example:
oEditor.CoverLines(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "TraceOutline", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"])
oEditor.ThickenSheet(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "TraceOutline", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"],
                     ["NAME:SheetThickenParameters", "Thickness:=", "0.035mm", "BothSides:=", False])
faces = oEditor.GetFaceIDs("CoaxDiel")
oEditor.DetachFaces(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "CoaxDiel", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"],
                    ["NAME:Parameters", ["NAME:DetachFacesToParameters", "FacesToDetach:=", [int(faces[0])]]])
oEditor.Section(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Region", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"],
                ["NAME:SectionToParameters", "CreateNewObjects:=", True, "SectionPlane:=", "YZ", "SectionCrossObject:=", False])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.modeler.thicken_sheet / cover_lines / cover_faces / detach_faces / section. The section command is oEditor.Section (menu name Section Along Plane); CreateObjectFromFaces / CreateObjectFromEdges copy faces/edges without detaching them.

tools.name: oEditor.AssignMaterial
tools.description: Assign a material to selected objects, together with the solve-inside, shell-element and material-appearance attributes - the native Modeler > Assign Material. Good conductors are typically assigned with SolveInside False so their interior is excluded from the mesh; the Selections array carries the PML-region flags recorded by the GUI.
tools.usage:
oEditor.AssignMaterial(["NAME:Selections", "AllowRegionDependentPartSelectionForPMLCreation:=", True, "AllowRegionSelectionForPMLCreation:=", True, "Selections:=", "Box1,Box2"],
                       ["NAME:Attributes", "MaterialValue:=", "\"copper\"", "SolveInside:=", False, "ShellElement:=", False, "ShellElementThickness:=", "nan", "IsMaterialEditable:=", True, "UseMaterialAppearance:=", False, "IsLightweight:=", False])

parameters.name: Selections
parameters.description: Comma-separated object names.

parameters.name: MaterialValue
parameters.description: Material name in escaped quotes; must exist in the project or a library (see oDefinitionManager.DoesMaterialExist).

parameters.name: SolveInside
parameters.description: False for conductors modelled by surface impedance, True for dielectrics.

parameters.name: ShellElement / ShellElementThickness
parameters.description: Treat sheets as shell elements of given thickness (2022 R1+).

tools.example:
oEditor.AssignMaterial(["NAME:Selections", "AllowRegionDependentPartSelectionForPMLCreation:=", True,
                        "AllowRegionSelectionForPMLCreation:=", True, "Selections:=", "Patch,Gnd,Pin"],
                       ["NAME:Attributes", "MaterialValue:=", "\"copper\"", "SolveInside:=", False, "ShellElement:=", False,
                        "ShellElementThickness:=", "nan", "IsMaterialEditable:=", True, "UseMaterialAppearance:=", False, "IsLightweight:=", False])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.assign_material(objects, material) or obj.material_name = "copper". Changing material through ChangeProperty (Geometry3DAttributeTab > Material) is equivalent for a single object.

tools.name: oEditor.ChangeProperty (Geometry3DAttributeTab: Material, Color, Transparent, Solve Inside, Model, Display Wireframe, Name)
tools.description: Edit object attributes shown in the Properties window: material, colour, transparency, solve-inside flag, model/non-model status, wireframe display and the object name. The call addresses one or more objects through PropServers and lists ChangedProps entries; it is the universal edit mechanism of the object model and what PyAEDT's Object3d property setters use.
tools.usage:
oEditor.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Geometry3DAttributeTab", ["NAME:PropServers", "Box1", "Box2"],
    ["NAME:ChangedProps",
     ["NAME:Material", "Value:=", "\"copper\""],
     ["NAME:Color", "R:=", 255, "G:=", 128, "B:=", 0],
     ["NAME:Transparent", "Value:=", 0.6],
     ["NAME:Solve Inside", "Value:=", False],
     ["NAME:Model", "Value:=", True],
     ["NAME:Display Wireframe", "Value:=", True],
     ["NAME:Name", "Value:=", "NewName"]]]])

parameters.name: PropServers
parameters.description: Object names to edit (several allowed for the same change).

parameters.name: Material
parameters.description: Escaped-quoted material name.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: R/G/B integers 0-255.

parameters.name: Transparent
parameters.description: 0 (opaque) to 1.

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: False turns the object into a non-model (not solved) object.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Renames the object (only one PropServer).

tools.example:
oEditor.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Geometry3DAttributeTab", ["NAME:PropServers", "Region"],
    ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:Transparent", "Value:=", 0.9], ["NAME:Display Wireframe", "Value:=", True]]]])
oEditor.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Geometry3DAttributeTab", ["NAME:PropServers", "Gnd"],
    ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:Material", "Value:=", "\"pec\""], ["NAME:Solve Inside", "Value:=", False]]]])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: obj.material_name, obj.color, obj.transparency, obj.solve_inside, obj.model, obj.display_wireframe, obj.name. Property names are the exact Properties-window labels; unknown labels are silently ignored, so verify with GetPropertyValue("Geometry3DAttributeTab", "Box1", "Material").

tools.name: oEditor.ChangeProperty (Geometry3DCmdTab: edit history commands - Position, XSize, Radius, Height, Padding)
tools.description: Edit the parameters of a command in an object's history tree (CreateBox, CreateCylinder, Move, DuplicateAroundAxis, CreateRegion ...) by addressing the PropServer as "<Object>:<Command>:<index>". This is how a script changes a box position or a region padding after creation without deleting and recreating the object, and how PyAEDT's history/command objects apply edits.
tools.usage:
oEditor.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Geometry3DCmdTab", ["NAME:PropServers", "Box1:CreateBox:1"],
    ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:Position", "X:=", "0.35in", "Y:=", "0.55in", "Z:=", "0in"], ["NAME:XSize", "Value:=", "10mm"]]]])
oEditor.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Geometry3DCmdTab", ["NAME:PropServers", "Region:CreateRegion:1"],
    ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:+Z Padding Data", "Value:=", "50mm"]]]])
props = oEditor.GetProperties("Geometry3DCmdTab", "Cylinder1:CreateCylinder:1")
val = oEditor.GetPropertyValue("Geometry3DCmdTab", "Cylinder1:CreateCylinder:1", "Radius")

parameters.name: PropServers
parameters.description: "Object:Command:Index" as shown in the history tree (index counts commands of the same name).

parameters.name: Position
parameters.description: Composite property with X/Y/Z sub-values; other properties use "Value:=".

parameters.name: GetProperties / GetPropertyValue
parameters.description: List the editable property names of a command and read one value (strings with units).

tools.example:
print(oEditor.GetProperties("Geometry3DCmdTab", "Box1:CreateBox:1"))
oEditor.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Geometry3DCmdTab", ["NAME:PropServers", "Box1:CreateBox:1"],
    ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:ZSize", "Value:=", "h_sub"], ["NAME:Position", "X:=", "-w/2", "Y:=", "-l/2", "Z:=", "0mm"]]]])
print(oEditor.GetPropertyValue("Geometry3DCmdTab", "Box1:CreateBox:1", "ZSize"))
tools.notes: PyAEDT: obj.history() returns the BinaryTreeNode of commands with .props and .update_property(); e.g. hfss.modeler["Box1"].history().children["CreateBox:1"].props["ZSize"] = "2mm". Assigning an expression makes the dimension variable-driven.

tools.name: oEditor.GetObjectsInGroup / oEditor.GetObjectName / oEditor.GetObjectIDByName / oEditor.GetNumObjects / oEditor.GetSelections
tools.description: Inventory queries of the modeler: object names by group ("Solids", "Sheets", "Lines", "Unclassified", "Non Model", a material name or a user group), the name for an object ID and vice versa, the total object count, and the objects currently selected in the GUI. They let a script discover what an interactively built model contains before assigning boundaries or exporting.
tools.usage:
names = oEditor.GetObjectsInGroup("Solids")         # or "Sheets", "Lines", "Unclassified", "Non Model", "copper", "MyGroup"
name = oEditor.GetObjectName(objectID)
oid = oEditor.GetObjectIDByName("Box1")
n = oEditor.GetNumObjects()
selected = oEditor.GetSelections()
names = oEditor.GetMatchedObjectName("Via*")

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Built-in group name, material name or user group; returns an array of object name strings.

parameters.name: objectID
parameters.description: Integer ID (from GetObjectIDByName or face queries).

parameters.name: GetMatchedObjectName
parameters.description: Wildcard match on object names.

tools.example:
for name in oEditor.GetObjectsInGroup("Sheets"):
    print(name, oEditor.GetObjectIDByName(name))
conductors = list(oEditor.GetObjectsInGroup("copper")) + list(oEditor.GetObjectsInGroup("pec"))
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("MeshSetup")
oModule.AssignSkinDepthOp(["NAME:Skin", "Objects:=", conductors, "RestrictElem:=", False, "NumMaxElem:=", 1000,
                           "SkinDepth:=", "2um", "SurfTriMaxLength:=", "1mm", "NumLayers:=", 2])
print(oEditor.GetNumObjects(), oEditor.GetSelections())
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.modeler.object_names / solid_names / sheet_names / line_names / unclassified_names, get_objects_in_group, get_obj_id, get_objects_by_name. Unclassified objects are bodies that failed to be classified after import or a bad boolean.

tools.name: oEditor.GetEdgeIDsFromFace / oEditor.GetVertexIDsFromEdge / oEditor.GetVertexIDsFromFace / oEditor.GetEdgeIDsFromObject
tools.description: Topology traversal by ID: the edges bounding a face, the vertices of an edge or a face, and all edges of an object. Combined with GetFaceIDs and the position queries they let a script walk from an object to the exact edge or vertex needed for an integration line, a terminal edge, a face coordinate system or a circuit port.
tools.usage:
edges = oEditor.GetEdgeIDsFromFace(faceID)
verts = oEditor.GetVertexIDsFromEdge(edgeID)
verts = oEditor.GetVertexIDsFromFace(faceID)
edges = oEditor.GetEdgeIDsFromObject("Box1")
faces = oEditor.GetFaceIDs("Box1")

parameters.name: faceID / edgeID
parameters.description: Integer IDs; all functions return arrays of ID strings/ints.

parameters.name: GetEdgeIDsFromObject
parameters.description: Every edge of the object (already catalogued with GetFaceIDs; listed here for the traversal chain).

tools.example:
face = int(oEditor.GetFaceIDs("PortSheet")[0])
edges = oEditor.GetEdgeIDsFromFace(face)
for e in edges:
    v1, v2 = oEditor.GetVertexIDsFromEdge(int(e))
    print(e, oEditor.GetVertexPosition(int(v1)), oEditor.GetVertexPosition(int(v2)))
# use the two end points of the shortest edge as an integration line
lengths = [(float(oEditor.GetEdgeLength(int(e))), int(e)) for e in edges]
shortest = min(lengths)[1]
p1, p2 = [oEditor.GetVertexPosition(int(v)) for v in oEditor.GetVertexIDsFromEdge(shortest)]
tools.notes: PyAEDT: face.edges, edge.vertices, obj.edges, hfss.modeler.get_face_edges / get_edge_vertices / get_object_edges. IDs are integers but often returned as strings through COM - cast with int().

tools.name: oEditor.GetFaceCenter / oEditor.GetVertexPosition / oEditor.GetFaceArea / oEditor.GetEdgeLength / oEditor.GetModelBoundingBox
tools.description: Metric queries: the centre of a planar face, the coordinates of a vertex, the area of a face, the length of an edge and the global bounding box of the whole model, all returned as strings with units in the model unit. They support choosing the right face for a port (e.g. the one with minimum x), sizing air regions from the model extent and checking imported geometry.
tools.usage:
center = oEditor.GetFaceCenter(faceID)          # ["x", "y", "z"] strings
pos = oEditor.GetVertexPosition(vertexID)
area = oEditor.GetFaceArea(faceID)
length = oEditor.GetEdgeLength(edgeID)
bb = oEditor.GetModelBoundingBox()               # [Xmin, Ymin, Zmin, Xmax, Ymax, Zmax]
units = oEditor.GetModelUnits()

parameters.name: faceID / vertexID / edgeID
parameters.description: Integer entity IDs.

parameters.name: return values
parameters.description: Numeric strings without unit suffix in model units (convert with float()).

tools.example:
faces = oEditor.GetFaceIDs("CoaxDiel")
xmin_face = min(faces, key=lambda f: float(oEditor.GetFaceCenter(int(f))[0]))
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignWavePort(["NAME:P1", "Faces:=", [int(xmin_face)], "NumModes:=", 1, "RenormalizeAllTerminals:=", True,
                        "DoDeembed:=", False, ["NAME:Modes", ["NAME:Mode1", "ModeNum:=", 1, "UseIntLine:=", False]]])
bb = [float(v) for v in oEditor.GetModelBoundingBox()]
print("model size:", bb[3]-bb[0], bb[4]-bb[1], bb[5]-bb[2], oEditor.GetModelUnits())
tools.notes: PyAEDT: face.center, vertex.position, face.area, edge.length, hfss.modeler.get_model_bounding_box(). GetFaceCenter fails on non-planar faces; use GetFaceCenter on planar faces only or PyAEDT's face.centroid.

tools.name: oEditor.GetFaceByPosition / oEditor.GetEdgeByPosition / oEditor.GetBodyNamesByPosition
tools.description: Position-based entity lookup: the face or edge of an object passing through a point, and the objects containing a point. These queries are what makes recorded scripts robust after re-import, because IDs change but coordinates do not; PyAEDT's get_faceid_from_position family wraps them.
tools.usage:
faceID = oEditor.GetFaceByPosition(["NAME:FaceParameters", "BodyName:=", "Box1", "XPosition:=", "0mm", "YPosition:=", "0mm", "ZPosition:=", "5mm"])
edgeID = oEditor.GetEdgeByPosition(["NAME:EdgeParameters", "BodyName:=", "Box1", "XPosition:=", "0mm", "YPosition:=", "0mm", "ZPosition:=", "0mm"])
names = oEditor.GetBodyNamesByPosition(["NAME:Parameters", "XPosition:=", "0mm", "YPosition:=", "0mm", "ZPosition:=", "1mm"])

parameters.name: BodyName
parameters.description: Object to search (required for face/edge lookup).

parameters.name: XPosition / YPosition / ZPosition
parameters.description: Point coordinates with units; the entity must pass through or contain the point within tolerance.

tools.example:
fid = oEditor.GetFaceByPosition(["NAME:FaceParameters", "BodyName:=", "Sub", "XPosition:=", "0mm", "YPosition:=", "0mm", "ZPosition:=", "h_sub"])
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignPerfectE(["NAME:PatchPEC", "Faces:=", [int(fid)], "InfGroundPlane:=", False])
print(oEditor.GetBodyNamesByPosition(["NAME:Parameters", "XPosition:=", "0mm", "YPosition:=", "0mm", "ZPosition:=", "h_sub/2"]))
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.modeler.get_faceid_from_position, get_edgeid_from_position, get_bodynames_from_position. A point on a shared face is ambiguous; give BodyName to disambiguate.

oEditor.Import(["NAME:NativeBodyParameters", "HealOption:=", 0, "Options:=", "-1", "FileType:=", "UnRecognized", "MaxStitchTol:=", -1,

    "Selections:=", "Box1,Box2", "File Name:=", "C:/work/export.step", "Major Version:=", -1, "Minor Version:=", -1])

tools.name: oEditor.SetModelUnits / oEditor.GetModelUnits
tools.description: Read or set the modeler length unit of the design (Modeler > Units). With Rescale False the numbers keep their values and change meaning; with Rescale True the geometry is scaled so physical sizes are preserved. Scripts that build geometry from unit-less numbers set the unit first.

oEditor.SetModelUnits(["NAME:Units Parameter", "Units:=", "mm", "Rescale:=", False])
units = oEditor.GetModelUnits()

parameters.name: Rescale
parameters.description: True multiplies all coordinates to keep the physical size.

tools.example:
oEditor.SetModelUnits(["NAME:Units Parameter", "Units:=", "mil", "Rescale:=", False])
print(oEditor.GetModelUnits())   # mil

tools.name: oEditor.Delete / oEditor.Copy / oEditor.Paste / oEditor.Undo / oEditor.Redo
tools.description: Object lifecycle and clipboard: delete selected objects (boundaries on them are removed too), copy objects to the clipboard and paste them into the same or another design (the mechanism behind copy_solid_bodies_from), and undo/redo the last modeler operations. Paste returns the names of the created objects, which may receive suffixes on name clashes.
tools.usage:
oEditor.Delete(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Box1,Sheet1"])
oEditor.Copy(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Patch,Sub"])
names = oEditor.Paste()
oEditor.Undo()
oEditor.Redo()

parameters.name: Selections
parameters.description: Comma-separated object names.

parameters.name: Paste
parameters.description: Pastes into the active editor; switch designs with oProject.SetActiveDesign and SetActiveEditor first for cross-design copies.

tools.example:
src = oProject.SetActiveDesign("RF"); ed1 = src.SetActiveEditor("3D Modeler")
ed1.Copy(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Housing,PCB,Trace"])
dst = oProject.SetActiveDesign("Thermal"); ed2 = dst.SetActiveEditor("3D Modeler")
new_names = ed2.Paste()
print(new_names)
ed2.Delete(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "OldRegion"])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.modeler.delete, hfss.modeler.copy / paste, hfss.copy_solid_bodies_from. Undo in a script undoes GUI-visible operations only; project-level undo is oProject.Undo().

tools.name: oEditor.CreateRelativeCS / oEditor.SetWCS / oEditor.EditRelativeCS
tools.description: Create a relative coordinate system by origin and X/Y axis vectors (Axis/Position mode) or by Euler angles, make a coordinate system the working one so later geometry and split/section planes use it, and edit an existing CS. Coordinate systems are the placement mechanism for components, arrays and radiation setups in scripts.

oEditor.CreateRelativeCS(["NAME:RelativeCSParameters", "Mode:=", "Axis/Position", "OriginX:=", "0mm", "OriginY:=", "0mm", "OriginZ:=", "0mm",
    "XAxisXvec:=", "1mm", "XAxisYvec:=", "0mm", "XAxisZvec:=", "0mm", "YAxisXvec:=", "0mm", "YAxisYvec:=", "1mm", "YAxisZvec:=", "0mm"],
    ["NAME:Attributes", "Name:=", "RelativeCS1"])
oEditor.SetWCS(["NAME:SetWCS Parameter", "Working Coordinate System:=", "RelativeCS1", "RegionDepCSOk:=", False])
oEditor.EditRelativeCS(["NAME:RelativeCSParameters", "Mode:=", "Euler Angle ZXZ", "OriginX:=", ..., "Psi:=", "0deg", "Theta:=", "30deg", "Phi:=", "0deg"], ["NAME:Attributes", "Name:=", "RelativeCS1"])

parameters.description: "Axis/Position" (X and Y axis vectors), "Euler Angle ZXZ", "Euler Angle ZYZ".

parameters.name: OriginX/Y/Z
parameters.description: Origin in the current working CS (the new CS is referenced to it).

parameters.name: XAxis*vec / YAxis*vec
parameters.description: Axis direction components (units are recorded but irrelevant).

parameters.name: Working Coordinate System
parameters.description: "Global" or a CS name for SetWCS.

tools.example:
oEditor.CreateRelativeCS(["NAME:RelativeCSParameters", "Mode:=", "Axis/Position", "OriginX:=", "x_feed", "OriginY:=", "0mm",
    "OriginZ:=", "h_sub", "XAxisXvec:=", "0mm", "XAxisYvec:=", "1mm", "XAxisZvec:=", "0mm", "YAxisXvec:=", "0mm",
    "YAxisYvec:=", "0mm", "YAxisZvec:=", "1mm"], ["NAME:Attributes", "Name:=", "FeedCS"])
oEditor.SetWCS(["NAME:SetWCS Parameter", "Working Coordinate System:=", "FeedCS", "RegionDepCSOk:=", False])
# ... draw in FeedCS ...
oEditor.SetWCS(["NAME:SetWCS Parameter", "Working Coordinate System:=", "Global", "RegionDepCSOk:=", False])

tools.usage:
oEditor.CreateUserDefinedPart(["NAME:UserDefinedPrimitiveParameters", "DllName:=", "HFSS/Antennas/Helix", "Version:=", "2.0", "NoOfParameters:=", 4, "Library:=", "syslib",

    ["NAME:InstanceParameters", "GeometryParameters:=", "patch_w='36mm'", "MaterialParameters:=", "", "DesignParameters:=", ""]])

oEditor.FitAll()

parameters.name: ComponentFile / TargetCS / GeometryParameters

oEditor.Insert3DComponent(["NAME:InsertComponentData", "TargetCS:=", "E0", "ComponentFile:=", "C:/lib/patch_element.a3dcomp",

tools.name: oDefinitionManager.AddMaterial
tools.description: Add a project-level material definition with simple, anisotropic or frequency/temperature-dependent properties: permittivity, permeability, conductivity, dielectric and magnetic loss tangents, thermal and mechanical properties, ferrite parameters (saturation magnetisation, Lande g, delta H) and appearance. Obtained from oProject.GetDefinitionManager(), it is the native form of Tools > Edit Libraries > Materials > Add Material and of PyAEDT's materials.add_material.
tools.usage:
oDefinitionManager = oProject.GetDefinitionManager()
oDefinitionManager.AddMaterial(["NAME:FR4_custom", "CoordinateSystemType:=", "Cartesian", "BulkOrSurfaceType:=", 1,
    ["NAME:PhysicsTypes", "set:=", ["Electromagnetic", "Thermal"]],
    "permittivity:=", "4.4", "dielectric_loss_tangent:=", "0.02", "thermal_conductivity:=", "0.3", "mass_density:=", "1850"])
# anisotropic property
["NAME:permittivity", "property_type:=", "AnisoProperty", "unit:=", "", "component1:=", "9.4", "component2:=", "9.4", "component3:=", "11.6"]
# thermal modifier
["NAME:ModifierData", ["NAME:ThermalModifierData", "modifier_data:=", "thermal_modifier_data", ["NAME:all_thermal_modifiers", ["NAME:one_thermal_modifier", "Property::=", "permittivity", "Index::=", 0, "prop_modifier:=", "thermal_modifier", "use_free_form:=", True, "free_form_value:=", "1+0.0004*(Temp-22)"]]]]

parameters.name: NAME:<material>
parameters.description: Material name (unique in the project; library materials of the same name are shadowed).

parameters.name: permittivity / permeability / conductivity / dielectric_loss_tangent / magnetic_loss_tangent
parameters.description: Electromagnetic properties as strings (expressions and dataset pwl() allowed).

parameters.name: thermal_conductivity / mass_density / specific_heat / youngs_modulus / poissons_ratio / thermal_expansion_coefficient
parameters.description: Thermal and structural properties used by Icepak/Mechanical links.

parameters.name: saturation_mag / lande_g_factor / delta_H
parameters.description: Ferrite parameters for gyrotropic materials with Magnetic Bias.

parameters.name: AnisoProperty
parameters.description: Sub-array with component1/2/3 for diagonal tensors; CoordinateSystemType may be Cartesian, Cylindrical or Spherical.

tools.example:
oDefinitionManager = oProject.GetDefinitionManager()
if not oDefinitionManager.DoesMaterialExist("Sapphire_aniso"):
    oDefinitionManager.AddMaterial(["NAME:Sapphire_aniso", "CoordinateSystemType:=", "Cartesian", "BulkOrSurfaceType:=", 1,
        ["NAME:PhysicsTypes", "set:=", ["Electromagnetic"]],
        ["NAME:permittivity", "property_type:=", "AnisoProperty", "unit:=", "", "component1:=", "9.4", "component2:=", "9.4", "component3:=", "11.6"],
        "dielectric_loss_tangent:=", "0.00002"])
oEditor.AssignMaterial(["NAME:Selections", "AllowRegionDependentPartSelectionForPMLCreation:=", True,
                        "AllowRegionSelectionForPMLCreation:=", True, "Selections:=", "Sub"],
                       ["NAME:Attributes", "MaterialValue:=", "\"Sapphire_aniso\"", "SolveInside:=", True, "ShellElement:=", False,
                        "ShellElementThickness:=", "nan", "IsMaterialEditable:=", True, "UseMaterialAppearance:=", False, "IsLightweight:=", False])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.materials.add_material(name) then property assignments; hfss.odefinition_manager gives the same handle. Frequency-dependent Djordjevic-Sarkar models are expressed with the "ModelName" / "dielectric_model_frequency" keys that the material editor records - capture them from the GUI.

tools.name: oDefinitionManager.DoesMaterialExist / EditMaterial / RemoveMaterial / GetProjectMaterialNames / GetInUseProjectMaterialNames / ExportMaterial
tools.description: The rest of the material commands on the definition manager: test whether a material is defined (project or library), edit an existing project material with a new property array, remove a project material, list project materials (all or only those used by objects) and export a material definition. Scripts use DoesMaterialExist before AddMaterial to avoid errors, and GetInUseProjectMaterialNames to keep the project tidy.
tools.usage:
exists = oDefinitionManager.DoesMaterialExist("FR4_custom")
oDefinitionManager.EditMaterial("FR4_custom", ["NAME:FR4_custom", "CoordinateSystemType:=", "Cartesian", "BulkOrSurfaceType:=", 1, ["NAME:PhysicsTypes", "set:=", ["Electromagnetic"]], "permittivity:=", "4.6", "dielectric_loss_tangent:=", "0.018"])
oDefinitionManager.RemoveMaterial("Scratch_mat")
names = oDefinitionManager.GetProjectMaterialNames()
used = oDefinitionManager.GetInUseProjectMaterialNames()
oDefinitionManager.ExportMaterial("FR4_custom", "C:/lib/fr4_custom.amat")

parameters.name: material name
parameters.description: Case-insensitive lookup in project and system/user libraries for DoesMaterialExist; the other commands act on project materials only.

parameters.name: property array
parameters.description: Full definition array as for AddMaterial (properties not listed revert to defaults).

tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.materials.exists_material / remove_material / material_keys / get_used_project_material_names; editing is done through Material property setters. Library (.amat) materials cannot be removed through the definition manager.

tools.name: oEditor.ExportModelImageToFile / oEditor.ExportImage
tools.description: Save a picture of the 3D modeler window - optionally with selected objects and field plots, axis/grid/ruler visibility, orientation and pixel size - to a JPG/PNG/BMP file. It is the native routine behind hfss.post.export_model_picture and the way headless scripts document the built model.
tools.usage: oEditor.ExportModelImageToFile("C:/work/model.jpg", 1600, 1200, ["NAME:SaveImageParams", "ShowAxis:=", "True", "ShowGrid:=", "True", "ShowRuler:=", "True", "ShowRegion:=", "Default", "Selections:=", "", "FieldPlotSelections:=", "", "Orientation:=", "isometric"])

parameters.name: file / width / height
parameters.description: Output path (extension selects the format) and size in pixels (0 = window size).

parameters.name: ShowAxis / ShowGrid / ShowRuler / ShowRegion
parameters.description: String booleans and "Default"/"True"/"False" for the region visibility.

parameters.name: Selections / FieldPlotSelections
parameters.description: Comma-separated objects and field plots to include ("" = current view).

parameters.name: Orientation
parameters.description: "isometric", "top", "bottom", "front", "back", "left", "right", "trimetric", "dimetric".

tools.example:
oEditor.FitAll()
oEditor.ExportModelImageToFile("C:/work/antenna_top.png", 1920, 1080,
    ["NAME:SaveImageParams", "ShowAxis:=", "False", "ShowGrid:=", "False", "ShowRuler:=", "False", "ShowRegion:=", "False",
     "Selections:=", "Patch,Sub,Gnd", "FieldPlotSelections:=", "Mag_E1", "Orientation:=", "top"])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.post.export_model_picture(...). In -ng sessions image export works from 2022 R2; earlier releases need a graphical session. The FieldsReporter module has ExportPlotImageToFile for plot-centred images.
